messages.author: a4c5d7d1c977b688
messages.subject: using NUTS in N-mixture models
parts:
Hi team,

Now I can use the NUTS sampler on continuous parameters (intercepts and slopes) while retaining other samplers on discrete parameters (in this case slice sampler on latent abundance) in N-mixture models (code attached). Everything looks great. For the same sample size and the same number of iterations, the NUTS sampler takes longer (72 seconds) than a MH sampler with block update (31 seconds), but the chains obviously are mixed much better for the former (attached). The only concern is that, even though it doesn't seem to cause any issues, I keep seeing this warning message when using the NUTS sampler (not for MH). I wonder if there is anything I can do to prevent this, or is it just fine?

Warning: slice sampler reached maximum number of contractions for 'N[21]'. Current parameter value is 8.
Warning: slice sampler reached maximum number of contractions for 'N[24]'. Current parameter value is 4.
Warning: slice sampler reached maximum number of contractions for 'N[55]'. Current parameter value is 2.

BTW, I can only do this on my personal computer, and am still waiting for helps to make this happen on my work computer.

Best, 
Qing

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: using NUTS in N-mixture models
parts:
Dear Qing,
Thanks for this report.
I believe things are working fine and the slice sampler is giving a false alarm. It is surprising that a case like this hasn't come up before. (Or, maybe it has but remained undiagnosed. Your small reproducible example is very helpful.)
Here is what I did (using N[53] as an example because that was among the last warning messages):
> compiled$model$y[53,]
[1] 3 1 2 1 2
> compiled$model$N[53]
[1] 3
> compiled$model$p[53,]
[1] 0.8414696 0.8484678 0.7847340 0.7212391 0.8531815
> compiled$model$lambda[53]
[1] 2.132799
> calcNodes <- model$getDependencies("N[53]")
> calcNodes
[1] "N[53]"    "y[53, 1]" "y[53, 2]" "y[53, 3]" "y[53, 4]" "y[53, 5]"
> Nvec <- 0:10
> lp <- numeric(11)
> for(i in 1:11) {
+ compiled$model$N[53] <- Nvec[i]
+ lp[i] <- compiled$model$calculate(calcNodes)
+ }
> lp
 [1]      -Inf      -Inf      -Inf  -8.85227 -14.59378 -21.52216 -29.14837
 [8] -37.25659 -45.72677 -54.48351 -63.47558
> 
So we can see that the shape of the conditional distribution for N[53] has a mode at 3 and decreases for each higher integer value. That makes sense (i.e. it is a plausible situation). I believe this can trigger the slice sampler warning because it goes through a scheme where first it steps out to the left and right of the current value (which in this case is also 3) and then makes draws, stepping in if it doesn't get a draw that falls within the slice (as determined by a randomly drawn auxiliary probability level for the slice). In this case this will result stepping in endlessly to 3-epsilon and 3+epsilon, if the slice level is such that only 3 is a valid next value for the node. Sorry, I know this explanation will only make sense if you know how the slice sampling works. Anyway, I am going to test a fix to catch this situation and then respond again if I make progress. 
In the meantime, please note from help(samplers) that you can turn off the warnings with a control parameter maxContractionsWarning=FALSE. (Of course, you wouldn't want to do that without believing they are harmless.) There will still be some wasted computation until I can make a better fix (if I am seeing the situation correctly).
Thanks for the report.
Perry

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: using NUTS in N-mixture models
parts:
Dear Qing,
I want to follow up on this issue from the fall. In our work on a new nimble version in December, I realized I had mis-diagnosed the problem you were encountering here. The slice sampler was working fine. The problem was a minor but verbose issue with nimbleHMC. On a handful of specific iterations during the HMC warm-up phase (the specific iterations being when specific steps happen during the warm-up schedule), it was possible for the model to be left in a state that would lead the slice sampler to not work as intended and hit the maximum number of contractions. We have also in December released an updated version of nimbleHMC that fixes this. If you are still working on this model, please try updating both nimble and nimbleHMC and see if the problem is resolved. The previous fix shouldn't have been necessary. Thanks for reporting the issue.
Perry
